findings.highlight: I will be able to endure this
findings.evidenceJa: なんとか我慢できそうです
findings.governingReading: Saber says she should somehow be able to endure, leaving the object conspicuously unstated.
findings.explanation: This supplies a definite object where her evasive phrasing is part of the hunger joke.

findings.evidenceJa: 早速昼食に致しましょう
findings.governingReading: Saber abruptly switches to the conspicuously formal 致しましょう, prompting Shirou to question her wording.
findings.explanation: The ordinary let us eat removes the local register shift on which the next reaction depends.

findings.highlight: Saber… you’re acting a bit strange.
findings.evidenceJa: 致しましょうって、セイバー……なんか、微妙に言葉遣い違くないか？
findings.governingReading: Shirou quotes Saber’s 致しましょう and asks whether her wording has subtly changed.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the observation to strange behavior and deletes the specific speech evidence.

findings.highlight: we’ll forget the boxed lunch and make something that’s easy to digest
findings.evidenceJa: 消化しやすい料理を作り直すから
findings.governingReading: Shirou personally offers to replace the boxed lunch by cooking something easier to digest.
findings.explanation: We pluralizes the cooking agency and forget weakens his explicit decision to abandon that menu and remake it.

findings.highlight: I’ll bring some tea with lunch
findings.evidenceJa: 弁当とお茶持ってくる
findings.governingReading: Shirou goes to fetch the already-made boxed lunches and tea for the dojo.
findings.explanation: Tea with lunch blurs the two concrete objects and weakens the branch’s prepared-versus-cooked distinction.
